samples.summary: New copy-refusal guard (`documentHasTableAtNestingCap`) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `document-copy.service.ts` now throws `BadRequestException('Cannot copy this document: it contains a table nested too deeply …')` before rewriting a copied document. Grepping `document-copy.service.spec.ts` for `Cannot copy this document`, `nested too deeply` and `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` yields no matches, and no other backend spec references the copy path's cap. Nothing pins either half of the contract: that a document at the cap is refused (rather than silently copied with rows dropped — the very data loss the guard exists to prevent), or that an ordinary nested-table document still copies. A regression here is silent data loss in a user-visible feature.
searchedFor: Grep 'Cannot copy this document|nested too deeply|documentHasTableAtNestingCap' in packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.spec.ts

samples.summary: The new `setHeader`/`setFooter` truncated-rows refusals are untested
samples.evidence: `setHeader` and `setFooter` gained refusal gates (`hasTableAtNestingCap(...) && this.replacesTruncatedRows(...)` → `warnDeclinedTruncatedRowsWrite`). The new test block in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` (`the write side carries the read side's nesting cap`) covers only `setDocument`, `insertBlockAfter`, `updateTableCell`, `updateBlock`, `insertTableRow`, `insertTableColumn`. Grepping that file for `declined`/`console.warn` returns nothing, and `setHeader` only appears at the three pre-existing tests (lines ~2017-2047). The footer gate additionally computes its path as `children.length - 1` off the live tree — an untested index. If either gate misfires, a header/footer edit either deletes a peer's rows (the exact bug the change targets) or silently declines every legitimate header edit.
searchedFor: Grep 'declined|warnDeclined|console.warn' in the same test file

samples.summary: Paste-path wiring of the nesting cap (insertBlocks / pasteTableCells) is only tested at the helper level
samples.evidence: `insertBlocks` now calls `capTableNesting(incoming, this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId))` and `pasteTableCells` computes `cellBaseDepth = this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) + (cellInfo ? 0 : 1)` before `capTableCellsNesting`. `packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts` exercises `capTableNesting`/`capTableCellsNesting` directly with hand-supplied base depths only; grepping the docs test tree for `capTableNesting|capTableCellsNesting|pasteTableCells` shows no test that pastes through the editor and observes what lands. So the depth-derivation (the `+1` for the not-in-a-cell branch, and using the caret block rather than the target cell) — the part that is easy to get wrong — cannot fail any test. A wrong base depth either drops tables from an ordinary paste (silent data loss) or writes past the cap (unreadable content).

samples.summary: The validation boundary change (`> MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` → `>= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`) is not pinned by any test
samples.evidence: `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` is also 32 (controller line 817), so the only behavioural difference this hunk makes is at depth exactly 32: previously accepted, now rejected. `docs-content.validation.spec.ts` tests only depth 20000 (rejected) and depth 2 (accepted) — both outcomes are identical before and after the change, so the entire hunk could be reverted with the suite still green. No test asserts `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH - 1` accepted / `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` rejected.

samples.summary: The revision-preview cap test cannot fail if the new adapter cap is removed
samples.evidence: `the revision-preview table-nesting cap` asserts `tableChainLength(parsed) === MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` for a 200-deep chain. `docsTreeToDocument` (unchanged in behaviour by this file) already truncates at the same cap, so deleting the new `normalizeYsonTreeNode` depth parameter entirely would leave both assertions passing. The test's own comment concedes this ("Isolating the adapter's own cap is not possible from out here by design"), so the added recursion bound in `snapshot-adapters.ts` ships with no test that can detect its absence.
searchedFor: Read the new describe block in snapshot-adapters.test.ts diff

samples.summary: Editor-level 'insert table in cell' refusal at the cap has no test
samples.evidence: `editor.ts` returns early when `doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, and the comment stresses it is checked *before* the split so no stray empty paragraph is left. Only the model backstop is tested (`insertTableInCell refuses to nest past the cap` in table-nesting.test.ts, asserting the throw). Grepping the docs test tree for `insertTableInCell|nesting cap|tableNestingDepth` finds only model tests — nothing asserts the editor command is a clean no-op (no split residue, no thrown error surfacing to the user).

samples.summary: Tab in the last cell of a table at the nesting cap (declined insertRow) is untested
samples.evidence: `moveToNextCell` now reads back the row after `insertRow` and returns false when it did not land, explicitly to avoid a `TypeError` when `Doc.insertRow` declines at the cap. `packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts` tests only the model-side decline (`insertRow and insertColumn decline at the nesting cap`); no view test presses Tab in the last cell of such a table, which is the path that previously crashed. New tests `rowless-table-nav.test.ts` and `cell-nav-cycle.test.ts` cover the rowless and cyclic cases but not this one.

samples.summary: No test proves the render path actually passes MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS
samples.evidence: `computeSelectionRects` and the two `getNormalizedRange` callers (`formatSourcePosition`, arrow-key collapse) were changed to pass the budget; `cell-range-expand.test.ts` only calls `expandCellRangeForMerges` directly with an explicit budget. If a caller were changed back to the exact default, no test would fail — the bounding of the per-paint/per-keystroke path, which is the stated purpose of the change, is unverified at its call sites.
searchedFor: Read the new describe block in packages/docs/test/view/cell-range-expand.test.ts

samples.summary: buildCellRangeRects' new clamp to the resolved layout table is untested
samples.evidence: The loop bounds were changed to `Math.min(end.rowIndex, tl.cells.length - 1)` / `tl.columnXOffsets.length - 1` as a backstop for a rectangle that `normalizeCellRange` could not clamp (table resolves in the layout but not in the model). The only clamp test — `clamps a peer-written cell rectangle to the table it names` in nested-table-cell-range.test.ts — goes through `normalizeCellRange`, so it exercises the other clamp; nothing constructs the mismatch case this backstop exists for.
searchedFor: Read nested-table-cell-range.test.ts clamp test in diff

samples.summary: Filler assertions in the cycle-guard test
samples.evidence: `expect(leafId).toBeDefined()` and `expect(typeof editor._getCursorForTest().blockId).toBe('string')` hold regardless of whether the cycle guard works (the setup already required leafId, and the cursor always carries a string id). The meaningful assertion is `expect(press(...)).toBeUndefined()`; the rest reads as coverage but cannot fail. Similarly `expect(out.end.rowIndex).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(rows - 1)` in cell-range-expand.test.ts restates the input rectangle.

finding.summary: New copy-refusal guard (`documentHasTableAtNestingCap`) has no test at all
finding.evidence: `document-copy.service.ts` now throws `BadRequestException('Cannot copy this document: it contains a table nested too deeply …')` before rewriting a copied document. Grepping `document-copy.service.spec.ts` for `Cannot copy this document`, `nested too deeply` and `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` yields no matches, and no other backend spec references the copy path's cap. Nothing pins either half of the contract: that a document at the cap is refused (rather than silently copied with rows dropped — the very data loss the guard exists to prevent), or that an ordinary nested-table document still copies. searchedFor: Grep 'Cannot copy this document|nested too deeply|documentHasTableAtNestingCap' in packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.spec.ts

verdict.reason: The finding claims the copy-refusal guard `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` has no test at all and that neither half of its contract is pinned. Both halves are pinned in `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.spec.ts:711-757`, a `describe('the table-nesting cap')` block whose own comment names `DocumentCopyService` as the caller it protects: `:731` writes and reads back a nested-table chain one level under the cap (ordinary document still copies), `:739` asserts a document with a table at the cap is refused, and `:745` asserts the same for the header branch. Those tests drive `writeDocsRoot` (`docs-tree.ts:376`), which calls the very function the finding names (`docs-tree.ts:250`). The copy path reaches that same guarded writer at `document-copy.service.ts:459`, with only URL rewriting in between (`rehostImages`, `:311-346` returns the same structure), so the graded impact — a cap document being "silently copied with rows dropped" — is impossible and is itself covered: removing the copy service's check at `:446` yields a thrown refusal from `writeDocsRoot`, not a silent lossy copy, and the copy is rolled back (`document-copy.service.spec.ts:384`). The only genuinely uncovered residue is whether that refusal surfaces as BadRequestException/400 with the "Cannot copy this document" wording instead of a generic Error/500 — a loud, contained, non-data-losing difference that does not meet this lens's major bar.

verdict.reason: The refusal gates are real: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1046-1054 (setHeader) and :1097-1103 (setFooter, path computed as children.length-1 off the live tree). No test exercises either. Repo-wide grep for warnDeclinedTruncatedRowsWrite/replacesTruncatedRows/hasTableAtNestingCap hits only the frontend store and a separate backend copy (docs-tree.ts, which has no header/footer setters) — no test file at all. The only frontend setHeader test calls are yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2017/2033/2047, plain paragraph headers with no table, so hasTableAtNestingCap is false and the gate is never entered; setFooter has no frontend test call. The new cap suite at test lines 3646-3979 covers only setDocument, insertBlockAfter, updateTableCell, updateBlock, insertTableRow, insertTableColumn. Indirect routes also come up empty: the only production callers are Doc.ensureHeader/ensureFooter (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:285-306), and grepping packages/frontend/tests for ensureHeader/ensureFooter returns nothing; the concurrent integration file and two-user helper seed header/footer via setDocument only; packages/docs tests exercise MemDocStore, not the Yorkie gate. Missing coverage over a guard whose misfire either deletes a peer's rows or silently declines every legitimate header/footer edit is a major test-adequacy gap.
